findings.claim: The README says the attribute is omitted on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework, so generated code is not always excluded from coverage. This only partly meets 'all generated code is decorated'. The conditional emission is a reasonable reading of the derived criterion that generated code must compile on every supported target framework. The ledger records no decision on this.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the README.md addition and the '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK' guards in the templates. Consumers targeting netstandard2.0 or net4x get no exclusion.

findings.claim: The existing verified generator snapshots under tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests were not updated in the hunks. The acceptance criteria require existing verified snapshots to be updated. If the snapshots were not regenerated, the snapshot tests will fail on the changed output.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests snapshot tests (the GenerationTests and similar verify-based suites) on the head. Any mismatch against the *.verified.cs files shows the snapshots are stale.

findings.claim: The TransformUtilities change to the brace newline for constrained nesting types alters generated output unrelated to the requirement. It is likely needed so the '#if' directive lands on its own line, but it changes the output for every constrained nesting type.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the snapshot tests that use generic nested types with constraints and check for diffs beyond the attribute lines.

interpretations.summary: Unconditional, no setting. Every generated formatter, resolver and helper class gets a guarded [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] (omitted under NETSTANDARD2_0/NETFRAMEWORK), with no opt-out property.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add an opt-out setting, for example a MessagePackGeneratorOptions or assembly-attribute flag. The templates emit the attribute only when it is enabled, which is on by default. Alternatively, the change would cover only formatters and leave the resolvers alone.
